question: Distinguish between a fixed budget and a flexible budget.
sources: Budgets and budgetary control: fixed and flexible budgets

points.label: Meaning
points.description: A fixed budget is prepared for one level of activity; a flexible budget is prepared for different levels of activity.
points.basis: Budgetary control: meaning of fixed and flexible budgets

points.label: Rigidity
points.description: A fixed budget does not change when actual activity changes; a flexible budget can be adjusted to the actual level reached.
points.basis: Budgetary control: nature of fixed and flexible budgets

points.label: Cost classification
points.description: A flexible budget needs costs split into fixed, variable and semi-variable; a fixed budget does not.
points.basis: Budgetary control: preparation of flexible budget

points.label: Comparison and control
points.description: A flexible budget allows a fair comparison of actual cost with the allowed cost at the actual level, so it is better for control; a fixed budget comparison can mislead when activity changes.
points.basis: Budgetary control: use of flexible budget for performance evaluation

points.label: Suitability
points.description: A fixed budget suits stable conditions where output can be forecast; a flexible budget suits businesses where demand or output varies.
points.basis: Budgetary control: conditions favouring each type
